source: Muse recheck of first-pass flags; apply through the belt (02 fact block -> 16 -> 04/05 remint), never in place

corrections.corrected_statement: Expect other drivers to make mistakes and respond with courtesy rather than treating their errors as personal attacks.
corrections.note: The courtesy and not personal part is on page 24, not page 23.

corrections.corrected_statement: You can control your response to traffic even though you cannot control the traffic or another driver's actions.
corrections.note: The full sentence starts on page 24 and ends on page 25.

corrections.corrected_statement: You should never pass on a hill or curve or at a railroad crossing or at an intersection or where signs prohibit passing or over solid lines or when entering a tunnel or bridge or over the posted speed limit.
corrections.note: Changed approach to a bridge or tunnel to entering a tunnel or bridge.

corrections.corrected_statement: Always signal before changing lanes soon enough to let other drivers know what you are going to do within one hundred feet.
corrections.note: Added the missing within one hundred feet requirement.

corrections.corrected_statement: If you are threatened with a side impact collision, brake or accelerate quickly whichever seems more likely to reduce the impact and sound the horn and swerve away while watching the traffic around you.
corrections.note: Braking choice depends on likelihood of reducing impact, traffic awareness applies to swerving.

corrections.corrected_statement: Older model motorcycles do not have self cancelling turn signals, so use caution when attempting to pass them and take extra time to make sure they see you.
corrections.note: Removed the unprinted inference that a flashing signal does not confirm a turn.

corrections.corrected_statement: When alcohol reaches the brain it first affects control of judgment and skill.
corrections.note: Removed claim about recognition timing that the page does not state.
